_comment: What a remote request is allowed to become on a machine that has offered
itself to Huginn. THE SINGLE SOURCE — three programs need to agree about
this and they are written in three languages:
the Compose desktop runner   (Kotlin, com.silencelen.huginn.device)
the headless runner          (Node,   client/huginn-device)
the daemon's pre-check       (Node,   server/appd/lib/devices.js)
The first two BUILD THE ARGV — they are the enforcement. The third only
decides whether to bother offering the work, so a person is told 'that
machine is locked' at the moment they ask rather than a minute later.
Kept declarative because the failure mode of drift is not a wrong pixel: a
runner that granted Bash where this file says look would be a silent hole in
the fence around somebody's personal computer, and nothing would look wrong.
scripts/gen-device-policy.js expands this into the Kotlin table, the headless
runner's embedded copy, and the case matrix both implementations are tested
against. server/appd/test/device-policy-cases.test.js fails if any of them has
drifted from this file — which is why deploy.sh cannot ship a drifted daemon.
GENERATE, the local-inference rung, added 2026-08-25 (Kvasir P2):
- SCOPES[0] and EXCLUSIVE. An exclusive rung matches only itself, both ways:
a generate device runs ONLY generate work, and generate work runs ONLY on a
generate device. Plain rank ordering would let `own` satisfy generate and a
claude engine would serve a local-model request — the silent substitution
this design bans in both directions.
- THE FLOOR. An unparseable scope floors to generate in all three programs:
a scope nobody can reason about may run nothing a claude device runs, and
no claude engine will ever serve generate. An ABSENT scope at registration
defaults to enrolDefault (look), not the floor — saying nothing means a
read-only claude device, as it always has.
- LOCK. Exclusive scopes IGNORE lockDropsTo: a locked generate device keeps
serving generate. The lock rule exists to stop unwatched MUTATION, and a
generate run touches no files and grants no tools, so there is nothing for
a lock to withdraw — and dropping generate to look would sideways-GRANT ask,
a claude mode this row has no engine for. The drop would widen, not narrow.
- ARGV. streamFlags + --model + --resume only. No tool flags (the shim has no
tools to grant or deny), no --append-system-prompt (no context leaves this
host for the serving box), no --effort. A REFUSED generate row still carries
the look argv: if a refused row ever spawned anyway, the engine would be
claude, so the argv it must not exceed is the read-only claude one.
- refusals.engine is said by a RUNNER whose engine cannot serve the mode
(desktop always; headless when conf.llm is unset). The policy cannot see
which binary sits at the far end, so that last fence lives in the runner
and is unit-tested per runner rather than matrix-tested. Said here so both
runners say the same words.
- Future scopes must DECIDE exclusivity explicitly: a rung left out of
exclusiveScopes inherits plain-rank semantics, silently.

look._comment: Note what is not here: no Bash. And it is DENIED as well as un-granted, because Claude Code's safe-Bash classification is content-dependent — two near-identical commands a minute apart were approved and then refused. From the far end that reads as a fence that works and then does not. Deny is deterministic.

refusals.locked: this machine is locked, so it is read-only until someone unlocks it
refusals.scope: this machine is set to {scope}, which cannot run {mode}
refusals.engine: this machine has no local model engine, so it cannot run generate
